confidence_notes: Food and drink anchors come from three web searches that returned aggregated indexes. Numbeo (undated snapshot, apparently 2025) gave cappuccino about EUR3.70, domestic draft beer about EUR3.43, an inexpensive meal about EUR10.3 and a mid-range meal for two about EUR51. MyLifeElsewhere (2026) gave cappuccino about $4.17 and a pint about $3.83. Expatistan gave a downtown-club cocktail of about 34 PLN, which is a thin, single-venue-style figure. I found no direct Gdansk source for wine by the glass. I set it from the local relationship to beer, at roughly 1.3-1.4x a beer, and kept it below the cocktail price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates from general knowledge for peak-season July, not from live listings, and carry the most uncertainty. The July 2026 summer peak can push hotel rates well above the annual average.
comparable_city_reasoning: Gdansk is priced as a mid-sized Polish tourist city, somewhat above the Polish average and below Warsaw and Krakow in some categories. Its Baltic coastal summer demand lifts July accommodation rates.
